## Access (SAFE method — never print the plaintext password)
Connect to .200 via the platform's ssh2 approach (decrypt `server.rootPasswordEnc` for server id `cmsc9l72y000ghl7iyd87u5ja` and pass it directly into the ssh2 Client password field without echoing/logging it; mirror lib/sftp.ts). ASSERT `hostname -I` contains `51.79.226.200` before EVERY command. Any `docker compose up` MUST use `--env-file prod.env`. If a step is classifier-blocked, stop and report what's needed.

## Investigate first (read-only)
- The existing auth: how customers/clients sign in and register today (the account/login + register pages in SoulPilates.Astro, the auth controller in SoulPilates.API, JWT issuance, the user/client model + password hashing). Determine whether "sign in/up" here is the CUSTOMER account area (booking/portal) — assume customer-facing unless the code says otherwise; note if admin login is separate.
- Whether any Google OAuth config already exists in prod.env / appsettings.

## Build (on the STAGING stack /opt/soulpilates-staging)
- Backend: a Google OAuth **authorization-code** flow — endpoints to start the flow and handle the callback, verify the Google token, then either sign in an existing user (matched by verified Google email) or **create a new account** (sign-up) linked to that email, and issue the SAME JWT the app already uses. Store a `googleId`/`authProvider` on the user so a Google account and a password account for the same email reconcile safely (don't create duplicates; don't let Google sign-in hijack a password account with an unverified email).
- Frontend: a "Continue with Google" button on BOTH the login and the register pages, styled to match Soul Pilates, that kicks off the flow. Handle the callback → land the user logged in.
- **Self-gate**: if the Google client id/secret aren't configured (env), hide the button and no-op the routes (mirror how a well-built app degrades) — exactly so this can ship dark until creds are added. Read the creds from config/env: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` (or the app's existing config convention) + the redirect URI.
- Rebuild the staging backend/frontend with `--env-file prod.env`; confirm the staging backend starts clean (NO IDX10703 crash-loop) and the routes register (401/302, not 500).

## Rules
- Do NOT deploy to Soul Pilates PROD — hand the exact prod deploy command back (the repo's `scripts/deploy-prod.sh`). Commit to a branch `feature/google-auth`, push to origin.
- Prod containers/DB untouched; verify https://soulpilates.com.vn stays 200 before and after.

## Board (Nxeon DB on THIS box /opt/nxeon)
CREATE a card on the Soul Pilates board (boardId `cmsavfvil000hhla4nlpuyge6`) in the In progress column (`cmsavfvin000khla4anofdbxt`), title "Google Sign-in & Sign-up", type FEATURE, and add a "Claude" comment describing the build, the branch, and — critically — the EXACT Google Cloud Console setup the user must do (create an OAuth 2.0 Client for soulpilates.com.vn, the Authorized redirect URI to register, and which env vars to set), plus the prod deploy command. Mechanics: node script in /opt/nxeon using PrismaClient (`db.card.create`, `db.cardComment.create`).

Report: SP auth model found, backend + frontend changes, how sign-up vs sign-in + account-linking works, the self-gate behavior, staging build/health, the exact Google Cloud Console setup + env vars required, and the prod deploy command.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Publish to PRODUCTION (soulpilates.com.vn). Run from /opt/soulpilates.
# Pulls the latest `main`, rebuilds the prod images, and recreates the two app
# containers. Requires a git remote (GitHub) so `main` reflects merged, tested
# work from staging.
#
# Usage:   scripts/deploy-prod.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set -euo pipefail
cd /opt/soulpilates

echo "!!  Deploying to PRODUCTION (live customers). Ctrl-C within 4s to abort."
sleep 4

echo "→ updating main…"
git checkout main
git pull --ff-only || echo "   (no remote configured yet — deploying current working tree)"

PROD_API_URL=$(grep -oP '(?<=^PUBLIC_API_URL=).*' prod.env)

echo "→ building backend:latest…"
docker build -t soulpilates/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .

echo "→ building frontend:latest (PUBLIC_API_URL=$PROD_API_URL)…"
docker build --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL="$PROD_API_URL" -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro

echo "→ recreating app containers…"
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend

echo "→ smoke test…"
sleep 6
code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://soulpilates.com.vn/api/settings || echo "000")
echo "   /api/settings → $code (401 = healthy)"
echo "✓ production updated."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  Soul Pilates — Build & Deploy (local VPS)
#
#  Rebuilds Docker images from the source tree in /opt/soulpilates and
#  hot-swaps the running backend + frontend containers without touching
#  MongoDB, Redis, RustFS, or GlitchTip.
#
#  Usage:
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh               # rebuild both
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh backend       # rebuild + restart backend only
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh frontend      # rebuild + restart frontend only
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

set -euo pipefail

REPO_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$REPO_DIR/prod.env"

# ── Load prod env for PUBLIC_API_URL ─────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    # Skip blanks and comments
    [[ "$line" =~ ^\s*$ || "$line" =~ ^\s*# ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" != *=* ]] && continue
    key="${line%%=*}"
    val="${line#*=}"
    export "$key"="$val"
  done < "$ENV_FILE"
fi

PUBLIC_API_URL="${PUBLIC_API_URL:-http://localhost}"

TARGET="${1:-both}"

log() { echo -e "\033[1;36m[deploy]\033[0m $*"; }
ok()  { echo -e "\033[1;32m[deploy]\033[0m $*"; }
err() { echo -e "\033[1;31m[deploy]\033[0m $*" >&2; }

build_backend() {
  log "Building backend image (soulpilates/backend:latest)…"
  docker build \
    -t soulpilates/backend:latest \
    -f "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile" \
    "$REPO_DIR"
  ok "Backend image built."
}

deploy_backend() {
  log "Restarting backend container…"
  docker compose -f "$REPO_DIR/docker-compose.prod.yml" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" \
    up -d --no-deps --force-recreate backend
  ok "Backend container restarted."
}

build_frontend() {
  log "Building frontend image (soulpilates/frontend:latest) with PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL…"
  docker build \
    --build-arg "PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL" \
    -t soulpilates/frontend:latest \
    -f "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile" \
    "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.Astro"
  ok "Frontend image built."
}

deploy_frontend() {
  log "Restarting frontend container…"
  docker compose -f "$REPO_DIR/docker-compose.prod.yml" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" \
    up -d --no-deps --force-recreate frontend
  ok "Frontend container restarted."
}

case "$TARGET" in
  backend)
    build_backend
    deploy_backend
    ;;
  frontend)
    build_frontend
    deploy_frontend
    ;;
  both|"")
    build_backend
    build_frontend
    deploy_backend
    deploy_frontend
    ;;
  *)
    err "Unknown target '$TARGET'. Use: backend | frontend | both"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

ok "Done. Running containers:"
docker ps --filter name=soulpilates-prod-backend --filter name=soulpilates-prod-frontend \
  --format "  {{.Names}}  {{.Status}}"
